sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The Applicant has filed this Application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for enlarging the Applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.
11208002230862/2023 registered with Ajidam Police Station, Rajkot City for the offences punishable under Section 255, 260, 406, 417, 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 472, 475, 120B, 114 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7(1)(2) of the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use)
Act, 2005.

2. Heard learned Advocate Mr. Hiteshkumar Vachani for the Applicant and learned APP for the Respondent - State.
3. Learned Advocate for the Applicant has submitted that the present Applicant has been falsely implicated in the present offence.

The only role attributed to the Applicant in the present offence is to the effect that he had acted as the mediator / consultant between the first informant and the other coaccused for the purpose of business transactions between them and, for that, the Applicant had Samrit Shelani Tansar vs State Of Gujarat on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71779052/
1 received Rs.22 Lacs towards consultation charges, which has NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5495/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined already been returned by the Applicant to the original first informant.

entities.text: Samrit Shelani Tansar vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The original first informant has also received the said amount and, by filing the Affidavit before this court, he has consented for the Applicant being enlarged on bail.

He further submitted that the present Applicant was not aware about the intention of the other coaccused and also the fact that the office of Matak Autonomous Council Dibrugarh,
Assam was the bogus office.
It was the Coaccused Nos. 4 to 6 who were instrumental for creating such bogus office.
He has further submitted that the Applicant has good reputation in the society and no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.

4. Per contra, learned APP Ms. Krina Calla has vehemently opposed the present application for grant of regular bail contending that the Applicant had played an active role in commission of the offence in question.
He has introduced the first informant with the other coaccused and had pocketed an amount of Rs.22 Lacs towards consultation charges.
Learned APP has therefore submitted that looking to the nature of offence, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the Application may be dismissed.
5. Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.

From the record, it appears that a forged office in the name and style of Matak Autonomous Council Dibrugarh, Assam (hereinafter referred to as "the Council / Matak Office") was created for commission of the prsent offence and a telephone call was made to the brother of the first infoarmant who was in the business of manufacture of Submersible Pumps and he was informed that the aforesaid Council / Matak Office was desirous of purchasing 65000 Submersible Pumps from him.
On the said pretext, several meetings had taken NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5495/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined place between the first informant, his brother and the accused persons.

It was the present Applicant who had taken the brother of the first informant to Guwahati and it was the present Applicant himself who had introduced the brother of the first informant to the other coaccused as being the office bearers of the said Council / Matak Office.
The present Applicant and his brother were made to pay the amount of Rs. 2,14,00,000/- towards security deposit and approval deposit.
A total sum of Rs. 4,30,00,000/- had been paid by the first informant and his brother to the accused persons for procuring the order in their favour.

The record also indicates that a forged Purchase Order in the name and style of the aforesaid Council / Matak Office (Bearing National Emblem),
was also given to the brother of the first informant.
On the basis of the said Purchase Order 5660 Water Pumps had been delivered by the first informant at the address given by the accused persons.
As per the understanding, the amount of consideration was required to be paid within 45 days from the date of receipt of the goods.
Since no payment was made, the first informant and his brother started asking for payment to the accused persons.

The brother of the first infoamant went to Guwahati to the office of the aforesaid Council / Matak Office for the purpose of payment and it was found that the said office was closed, and therefore, the brother of the first informant had gone to the head office of the said Council / Matak Office where the Purchase Order, which was given to the first informant, was shown by his brother to the officers of the aforesaid Council / Matak Office and he was informed that the said Purchase Order was not genuine and the same was also not issued by Samrit Shelani Tansar vs State Of Gujarat on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71779052/
2 their office.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. From the record it appears that the entire fraud runs into the amount of Rs.18,88,75,000/- out of which the present Applicant had recived the sum of Rs.22 Lacs as per his own statement as concultation charges which has also been repaid by him to the original first informant.

6.1 The fact that the Applicant has returned the amount of Rs.22 Lacs  
 R/CR.MA/5495/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024  u indicates the complicity of the present Applicant in the offence in question.
7. Considering the aforesdaid aspects, no case if made out for exercising the discretion in favour of the Applicant.
The Application is dismissed.
(M. R. MENGDEY,J) J.N.W / 129
